claims: NASA's Artemis II mission is currently scheduled for launch no earlier than April 2026.
Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed flight.
Artemis II mission tests the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II mission tests the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II mission uses a free-return trajectory around the Moon.
Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II astronauts travel farther into space than ever before.
Artemis II launches from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center.
Artemis II launches on the SLS rocket.

Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) pushes Artemis II crew toward the Moon.
Artemis II includes a four-day journey to the Moon.
Artemis II includes a loop around the far side of the Moon.
Artemis II free-return trajectory allows gravity to guide the spacecraft back.
Artemis II crew demonstrates manual flying.
Artemis II crew demonstrates proximity operations.
Artemis II crew tests life-support systems.
Artemis II concludes with high-speed reentry into Earth's atmosphere.
Artemis II targets splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II is the first crewed mission of the Artemis program.
Artemis II validates the safety of the Orion capsule and its environmental systems for future lunar landings starting with Artemis III.
Artemis II crew travels 250,000 miles.
Artemis II tests human physiological responses to deep space including radiation.
